free_tier.stated: Registration of a template, launching a private copy from the Agent Marketplace and publishing a listing cost nothing; compute bills per second only while a sandbox is running, and without account balance or credit a sandbox stops a few seconds after launch. No recurring free sandbox allowance is published.
free_tier.notes: The vendor's overview states 'Registering costs nothing until you launch a sandbox' and the SDK limits page states that a sandbox without balance or credit stops within seconds. No free tier of running compute is published; a 24-hour default lifetime and 7-day paused retention are limits, not a free allowance. A promotional 12-hour free unlimited GLM 5.2 offer appears in a vendor social post and is not a standing tier.

per_object_cap.stated: about 500 MB per sandbox file upload; larger uploads return 413
per_object_cap.notes: The cap is on a single upload to a sandbox, not a stored-object quota; command stdout and stderr each return at most 1 MiB.

retention.stated: a running sandbox has a default lifetime of 24 hours if timeout_seconds is not set; a paused sandbox is kept for up to 7 days and then deleted with its disk
retention.notes: The 7 days apply to paused sandboxes; a running sandbox's default is 24 hours and both can be changed with set_timeout or resume.

egress.terms: sandboxes use a shared data center outbound IP; some sites block cloud IPs, and GMI offers an allowlist or a dedicated egress IP on contact. No included outbound byte allowance is published.

interface_detail: Python and Go SDKs and a REST control plane at https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1/agents; sandboxes were launched through POST /v1/containers and expose their own endpoint. The Agent Marketplace is used through the browser console, with interactive shell over a WebSocket data-plane host.
tooling: gmi-agentbox-sdk Python package and github.com/GMISWE/agentbox-sdk-go Go module; a GMI_AGENTBOX_API_KEY created in the Compute panel's API Keys page is required. Docker is not available inside a sandbox.
chaining: A sandbox runs a container image that binds an internal port and can call GMI models through one API key and one bill; model tokens bill through MaaS and sandbox compute bills per second, so a long-running worker needs its state checkpointed outside the sandbox to survive the 24-hour default lifetime or the 7-day paused expiry.

limits.value: an API key and a funded account are required: a sandbox without balance or credit stops a few seconds after launch; template registration and marketplace listing need a console account
24-hour default sandbox lifetime; paused sandboxes deleted after up to 7 days with their disk
about 500 MB per upload; larger returns 413; stdout and stderr each return at most 1 MiB
429 on too many requests; a synchronous execute waits at most 25 seconds and each HTTP request times out after 30 seconds by default

limits_note: One shell connection at a time per sandbox; a build artifact or a container image must be in a registry GMI can pull from. Hosted agents use a Container tier of 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 10 GiB ephemeral and 30 GiB data storage, billed per second; the vendor blog gives a worked planning figure of about USD 0.06 per container-hour.
binding_note: The funded-account gate binds first: template registration is free but a sandbox stops within seconds unless the organization has credit, before any lifetime or upload cap is reached.

identity_cost.detail: A GMI Cloud Console account, created with email and password or Google, GitHub or Hugging Face sign-in, and a GMI_AGENTBOX_API_KEY created in the Compute panel's Access > API Keys page are needed; a sandbox additionally needs balance or credit. No phone or identity document is stated on the pages read.

reliability_note: A sandbox with no credit stops within seconds of launch; the shared data center egress IP is blocked by some sites; a paused sandbox is deleted with its disk after up to 7 days and a running one has a 24-hour default lifetime; 429 rate-limit and 5xx server errors are returned without SDK retries.
confidence_note: The billing shape, account gate, sandbox and paused lifetimes, upload cap, egress address, console signup fields and API base were read from first-party vendor pages on 2026-11-24; the per-container-hour planning figure is from a vendor blog's worked example, not a published rate card.
